facts.statement: Koreanosaurus is a small, bipedal dinosaur belonging to the Orodrominae subfamily that lived in South Korea during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Koreanosaurus () is a genus of orodromine neornithischian dinosaur that lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous of what is now South Korea.

facts.statement: Koreanosaurus was a relatively small dinosaur with a body length of 2 to 2.4 meters.
facts.quote: Koreanosaurus was a relatively small dinosaur, reaching 2 - 2.4 m in body length.

facts.statement: Researchers believe Koreanosaurus was a burrowing dinosaur based on its close relatives and fossil evidence of small burrows found in the same geological layer.
facts.quote: Based on its taxonomic position and the existence of small burrows from the Seonso Conglomerate, Koreanosaurus is likely a burrowing dinosaur.

facts.statement: Unlike most of its relatives in the Orodrominae group, Koreanosaurus is assumed to have lived on all fours as a quadruped.
facts.quote: Unlike its orodromine relatives, Koreanosaurus is assumed to have been a quadruped.

facts.statement: Three specimens of Koreanosaurus were discovered in 2003 in the Seonso Conglomerate near the Bibong-ri dinosaur egg site on the southern coast of the Korean Peninsula.
facts.quote: In 2003, three specimens of Koreanosaurus were found in the Upper Cretaceous Seonso Conglomerate from the southern coast of the Bibong-ri dinosaur egg site, Boseong, Korean Peninsula.

facts.statement: The species was named Koreanosaurus boseongensis to honor the Boseong site 5 where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The type species was named after its locality (Boseong site 5).

facts.statement: The genus was first described in a 2008 master's thesis by Dae-Gil Lee and officially published in 2011 by a team including Min Huh and Pascal Godefroit.
facts.quote: This taxon was initially named and described in a master's thesis by Dae-Gil Lee in 2008, and was officially published by Min Huh, Dae-Gil Lee, Jung-Kyun Kim, Jong-Deock Lim and Pascal Godefroit in 2011.

facts.statement: Modern phylogenetic analyses consistently classify Koreanosaurus as a member of the family Thescelosauridae within the subfamily Orodrominae.
facts.quote: Subsequent phylogenetic analyses by researchers including Han et al. consistently classified Koreanosaurus as a member of Thescelosauridae, specifically within the subfamily Orodrominae.

facts.statement: Koreanosaurus lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Some researchers have suggested that Koreanosaurus might belong to the family Jeholosauridae or be closely related to it, though this is debated.
facts.quote: In 2012, Han et al. found it plausible that Koreanosaurus might be a member of Jeholosauridae or closely related to it.

facts.statement: The family classification for Koreanosaurus is uncertain, with some sources listing it as potentially belonging to Jeholosauridae.
